transcript: Last night I saw What Became of Us at Atlantic Theater Company. In this play, two siblings played by Rosalind Chao and BD Wong, recount their stories of growing up together. The older sibling was born in what they call “The Old Country” and the younger sibling was born here in the United States. Through a series of often one-liner anecdotes, we get a portrait of the inner dynamics of an immigrant family and the tensions that arose from the different mindsets of the siblings based on their differing experiences. The ensuing conflicts described here are the most interesting aspects of the play but I wish they had gone even deeper. This production is actually double cast with some performances featuring Sholeh Aghdashloo and Tony Shalhoub. This double casting suggests to me that the play is meant to speak to an experience of many immigrant families, but for a 75 minute two character play I think I would have preferred specificity. Though I found the writing stylistically sleek and poetic, the story felt kind of surface level to me and I thought the last third of it was more or less a series of cliches. But I could be the minority here as people in the audience seemed genuinely moved and I did notice people wiping tears during the curtain call, so feel free to take my thoughts with a grain of salt. With that, another program for my collection.
